content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral table, and all six figure briefs, and built the ledger item by item.

input.summary:
Full source ledger built and traced. Every limitation of all 20 claims (device 1-10, system 11-15, method 16-20), every one of the 17 numbered parts (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48), every sentence of the Field, Background, Summary, Brief Description of the Drawings, Detailed Description and Abstract, and all six figure briefs (FIG. 1 perspective, FIG. 2 section on 2-2, FIG. 3 bottom plan, FIG. 4 enlarged section on 4-4, FIG. 5 pulling element, FIG. 6 stirring elements) were checked against the affirmative inventor sources.

Traced to disclosure.md: rigid base with first and second sides; vibration motor coupled to the first side; air-extraction mechanism "such as a vacuum pump" coupled to the first side and "in fluid communication with a chamber located on a second side"; perimeter "formed as a rigid loop or skirt made from a low-friction material such as plastic, metal, PTFE, or a combination of rigid materials"; "not intended to form a complete airtight seal and does not rely on flexible rubber or foam"; "restricts airflow into the chamber while maintaining rigid contact with the tile"; "continuously removes air entering beneath the rigid perimeter, maintaining the chamber at a lower pressure than the surrounding atmosphere" (supports the clearance 34 beneath the bearing face, the volumetric-extraction-rate recitation and the continuous-running recitations); "holds the device firmly against the tile without requiring the operator to press downward"; "connected to the tile through rigid components... substantially less damping" (supports the all-rigid vibration transmission path and the exclusion of elastomeric, foam and resilient-mount members); "the low-friction perimeter allows the device to slide freely across different areas of the tile while the vacuum continuously maintains contact" (supports slidability, translating while the differential is maintained, and delivery to successive areas); "one or more handles used primarily for guiding"; "a rope, wire, cable, or similar flexible pulling element" and the decoupled-control passage; and the tile/bonding-material/substrate stack with trapped air, distribution, contact area and bond strength. Traced to the affirmative USER conversation passage: autonomous mode, "small stirring elements", and vibration causing "a constant forward motion" (Field clause, claim 10, third embodiment, FIG. 6). Formalities traced to brief.md: title verbatim, "Not applicable." in both cross-reference and government-support sections, three statutory classes, no means-plus-function recitals.

Internal consistency verified: claims and description use identical relationships and terms (bearing face as end face, clearance along at least part, chamber bounded by second side, perimeter member and exposed face); each numeral denotes exactly one part and every table numeral appears on at least one sheet and in the description; every figure brief matches its Brief Description entry, including the FIG. 2 enumeration of sectioned bodies against the hatched slab, legs and band with the housing in plain outline; the section-line designations 2-2 and 4-4 are repeated identically in FIG. 3's geometry (numeral 2 at both ends, numeral 4 at both ends), in the FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 briefs, in the Brief Description, and in the Detailed Description; hatching directions are consistent between FIG. 2 and FIG. 4; and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction to a person or unresolved alternative remains in any application section. Depiction conventions (rectangular slab, band, ring frame, blocks, cord path, port gap) stay confined to the figure briefs, are marked schematic there, add no undisclosed proportion, taper, angle, depth ranking or contact topology, and are not verbalized as broadening examples in the application text.

One item did not trace: claim 15 requires a single system embodiment having both the flexible pulling element and stirring elements, a combination no affirmative passage describes.

findings.title: Claim 15 requires a system having both a flexible pulling element and stirring elements, a combination no source passage describes
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md, claim 15 (dependent on claim 11); cf. draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Embodiment with stirring elements"
findings.detail: Claim 11 positively requires "a flexible pulling element connected to the vibration device" and recites that the device's "position ... is controlled by tension applied to the flexible pulling element". Claim 15 adds stirring elements to that same system, so the claim covers one embodiment carrying both features. The only affirmative inventor support for stirring elements presents them as the substitute for pulling, not as an addition to it, and no passage in the disclosure, in the conversation, or in the draft's own description discloses a device that both is drawn by a pulling element and carries stirring elements. The device-claim counterpart is correctly split: claim 9 (pulling element) and claim 10 (stirring elements) are separate dependents of claim 1 and never combine. Every other limitation of claims 1-20 traced to an exact affirmative passage.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "15. The system of claim 11, wherein the vibration device further comprises one or more stirring elements." Nearest source (input/conversation.md, USER): "the device is already connected via vaccum and unlike other machines it is free to move, so we don't even need to pull or move it with the hand, we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion". Draft's own description of the same embodiment (draft/08-detailed-description.md): "A third embodiment, shown schematically in FIG. 6, provides for autonomous movement. The vibration device 10 carries one or more stirring elements 48. The vibration produced by the vibration motor 18 may cause a constant forward motion of the vibration device 10, so that the vibration device 10 need not be pulled or guided by hand". No affirmative passage anywhere describes a pulling element and stirring elements on the same device.
findings.fix: Replace claim 15 with a limitation that traces to an affirmative passage about the system as claimed, e.g.: "15. The system of claim 11, wherein the air-extraction mechanism is a vacuum pump operable to withdraw air from the chamber continuously while the vibration device is in use." (supported by "An air-extraction mechanism, such as a vacuum pump" and "The air-extraction mechanism continuously removes air entering beneath the rigid perimeter"). Alternatively, cancel claim 15 and renumber claims 16-20 as 15-19, updating the dependencies in the renumbered claims 16-19 to refer to claim 15. Do not add description matter about a combined pulling-element-plus-stirring-element embodiment, as no source supports it.
